instruction: Apply only the supplied DSA guidance. Classify whether each proposed artifact is structurally ready for its stated lifecycle point. A design-system handbook must remain the primary artifact, application scenes must be supplemental and last, adoption must bind the current Design Authority identity, and target-declared conditions must not be replaced by a global template. Never infer aesthetic suitability from structure, hashes, rendering or completeness: human or validly delegated aesthetic selection remains required in every case.

facts: The entry navigation contains six polished application pages and no primary Token, component-contract or relationship-contract sections.
The pages introduce local button and card variants that are not indexed by the proposed system catalogue.
The author calls the result a design-system showcase.
The proposed handbook lists colors, type sizes, spacing values and component screenshots.
It omits visible-surface versus hit-target, type-occupancy, internal-padding versus line-height, group-gap versus item-gap, accent-allocation and containment relationship contracts.
Its component section has no anatomy, states, accessibility or do/don't contract.
Open Design produced a structurally complete candidate handbook.
No user or validly delegated selector selected the candidate and no separate Authority adoption was confirmed.
The HTML and sidecar label the candidate adopted.
The handbook previously matched the adopted Design Authority.
DESIGN.md was materially revised and now has a different current closure digest and human revision.
The showcase sidecar still binds the prior digest and revision.
The selected targets declare a desktop keyboard condition, a narrow embedded condition, 175% text scaling, one long localized label and reduced motion.
The review instead ran a generic 320/375/390/430 mobile screenshot list and did not exercise the declared desktop, text-scale, localization or motion conditions.
Static section presence passed.
The primary entry is an engineering design-system handbook with the complete adopted Token families, component catalogue and component/relationship/behavior/provenance contracts.
Application scenes are last, marked supplemental-validation, reuse the indexed components and introduce no second primitive system.

The inert local projection binds the current Design Authority closure digest and human revision, has no external network dependency, and the project's reproducible route exercised every target-declared material condition.
The machine checks are being asked only for structural artifact readiness, not an aesthetic verdict.
The handbook is otherwise complete and binds the current Authority digest.
Its typography and component examples load a remote stylesheet and a remote script at runtime.
Those resources are not local manifest-bound inert assets.
A candidate handbook is structurally complete, handbook-first and has supplemental application scenes last.
It preserves accepted, rejected and unresolved preference sets and exposes all target-declared review conditions.
Two aesthetically material unresolved choices remain and neither a human nor an explicitly delegated selector has selected this candidate.
No project Authority files have been changed.
